newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Commodity Price Index falls in September - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ Commodity Price Index falls in September - ANZ.

text.p: The average New Zealand dollar price of the country's commodity exports fell one percent in September 1996 following a 0.3 percent fall in August, ANZ Banking Group (New Zealand) Ltd said on Friday.
The corresponding average world price of New Zealand's commodity exports rose in September by 0.3 percent, compared with a 0.2 percent fall in August.

The New Zealand dollar index fell to 99.3 in September from 100.3 in August, down 10.1 percent on an annual basis, while the world price index rose to 122.5 from 122.1 over the same period, down 2.9 percent annually.

ANZ said the strong New Zealand dollar continued to account for the lacklustre performance of commodity prices measured in NZD terms. Overall, however, commodity prices remained flat, as the prospects of a quick recovery in key world markets remained some way off.

ANZ said commodity price trends over the past month or so had been somewhat mixed. Prices for wool, lamb, skins and sawn timber had each risen slightly in world markets. Dairy prices had deteriorated slightly for most commodities, with the exception of cheese, while aluminium prices also weakened.
On an annual basis, lamb, skins and apples were the only commodities showing a sustained improvement in New Zealand dollar prices compared with a year ago.
